Guideline: Split Dynamic and Static Canvas
Description: Prevent full canvas rebuilds
Do: Separate animated HUD/counters from static background/frames
Don't: Single canvas for entire UI
Code Bad: One giant Canvas containing 50 elements where 1 changes every frame

Guideline: Disable Raycast Target on non-interactive elements
Description: Reduce GraphicRaycaster CPU spikes
Do: Uncheck Raycast Target on text/images/decorations
Don't: Leaving Raycast Target ON for everything
Code Bad: Text and decoration images with raycastTarget = true

Guideline: Apply juicy tactile feedback on button clicks
Description: Give game feel with scale tween and sound
Do: Add juice: punch scale ~1.1x and settle back to 1.0x on pointer down, kill the previous tween first so rapid taps never compound, and play SFX
Don't: Static button that just changes color or does nothing
Code Bad: Unity standard color tint only

Guideline: Handle Device Notch and Safe Area
Description: Prevent UI overlap with notch/island
Do: Use Safe Area helper script to clamp RectTransform
Don't: Hardcode anchor to screen edge
Code Bad: RectTransform anchor 0-1 on iPhone with Dynamic Island

Guideline: Use Sprite Atlas and 9-Slice Slicing
Description: Keep drawcalls low and sharp borders
Do: Pack UI sprites into SpriteAtlas and set 9-slice borders on buttons
Don't: Raw uncompressed PNGs and scaled non-sliced images
Code Bad: Stretched non-sliced button with blurry corners

Guideline: Use TextMeshPro with SDF and Outlines
Description: Sharp text at any scale with game aesthetic
Do: Use TextMeshProUGUI with outline/underlay baked into a shared Material Preset (Unity 6: TMP ships inside com.unity.ugui)
Don't: Standard Legacy Text component
Code Good: TextMeshProUGUI using shared material preset 'Title_Outline' (Outline 0.2 + Underlay)
Code Bad: Legacy UnityEngine.UI.Text; or tmp.fontMaterial.SetFloat(...) per label (creates a material instance and breaks batching)

Guideline: Modal Dialog Popup with Dimming Overlay
Description: Clear visual focus for game dialogs
Do: Modal popup with 60% black overlay and bounce-in animation
Don't: Dialog without dim background competing with game board
Code Bad: Dialog placed directly over active game board

Guideline: Limit UI DrawCalls (draw calls) to under 15 batches
Description: Prevent UI from dominating frame render budget
Do: Keep batching intact: group elements using the same material/atlas and avoid Z-order interleaving; check batch count in the Frame Debugger
Don't: Alternating text and images causing batch breaks
Code Bad: Image then Text then Image causing 20 batches

Guideline: Show Floating Reward Numbers (+100 Gold)
Description: Reward perception and reinforcement
Do: Spawn pooling floating text with upward float and fade-out
Don't: Updating static text counter immediately without animation
Code Bad: coins += 100 with no visual popup

Guideline: Touch Target Size >= 48x48dp on Mobile
Description: Prevent mis-taps on small phone screens
Do: With CanvasScaler reference width 1080 (~3x density), keep tappable rects >= 144x144 units (48dp; iOS 44pt = 132)
Don't: Tiny close buttons (64x64 units on a 1080-wide reference is only ~21dp)
Code Good: Button RectTransform sizeDelta >= (144, 144) at 1080x1920 reference resolution
Code Bad: Tiny 'X' button in modal corner

Guideline: Set the CanvasScaler reference resolution for portrait games
Description: One canvas scaler layout from 16:9 and 21:9 phones to 3:4 tablets
Do: CanvasScaler: Scale With Screen Size, reference resolution 1080x1920, Screen Match Mode Expand so the reference area always fits (Match Width Or Height = 0 clips vertical content on 3:4 tablets); check 9:16, 9:21 and 3:4 in Device Simulator
Don't: Constant Pixel Size on a mobile game canvas
Code Good: canvasScaler.uiScaleMode = CanvasScaler.ScaleMode.ScaleWithScreenSize; canvasScaler.referenceResolution = new Vector2(1080, 1920); canvasScaler.screenMatchMode = CanvasScaler.ScreenMatchMode.Expand;
Code Bad: Constant Pixel Size: buttons shrink on 1440p phones and overflow on 720p

Guideline: Pool ScrollRect list cells (scroll list pooling)
Description: Long shop/leaderboard scroll lists stay at 60 FPS without GC spikes
Do: Instantiate only the visible cells plus one spare row and recycle them while the ScrollRect scrolls; clip with RectMask2D
Don't: Instantiate one prefab per item (hundreds of cells) under a VerticalLayoutGroup + ContentSizeFitter
Code Good: Recycling pool of ~12 cells repositioned in onValueChanged of the ScrollRect
Code Bad: foreach (var item in items) Instantiate(cellPrefab, content)

Guideline: Hide a canvas with Canvas.enabled, not SetActive
Description: Toggling panels without rebuilding batches
Do: Disable the Canvas component (it stops issuing draw calls but keeps its vertex data, so showing it again needs no rebuild) and its GraphicRaycaster so hidden buttons cannot take taps
Don't: gameObject.SetActive(false/true) on a large panel every time it opens (OnDisable/OnEnable + full rebuild)
Code Bad: shopPanel.SetActive(false);

Guideline: Cut UI overdraw from invisible and full-screen images
Description: Fill rate is the GPU bottleneck on mobile UI
Do: Disable Images that are fully transparent: with Cull Transparent Mesh on (the default for new components) they skip drawing but still take raycasts and rebuild cost, and with it off they still render; avoid stacking full-screen panels and stop rendering the 3D scene behind an opaque full-screen menu; inspect with the Scene view Overdraw mode
Don't: Transparent full-screen Image used only as a click blocker or fade layer left enabled
Code Good: Disable the fade Image when the tween completes; camera.enabled = false behind an opaque full-screen menu
Code Bad: Image color alpha = 0 left active over the whole screen

Guideline: Debounce taps on purchase and reward buttons
Description: Stop double purchase / double reward claim from a fast double tap
Do: Set button.interactable = false on the first tap and restore it only after the action completes, with a cooldown of at least 1000 ms
Don't: Calling the purchase or claim logic on every onClick with no guard
Code Good: buyButton.interactable = false; try { await PurchaseAsync(); } finally { await Awaitable.WaitForSecondsAsync(1f); buyButton.interactable = true; }
Code Bad: buyButton.onClick.AddListener(Purchase) with no interactable guard

Guideline: Use InputSystemUIInputModule on the EventSystem
Description: UI taps work when the project uses the Input System package
Do: Replace StandaloneInputModule with InputSystemUIInputModule on the EventSystem when Active Input Handling is Input System
Don't: Keeping StandaloneInputModule with Active Input Handling = Input System only (it throws and UI ignores taps)
Code Bad: EventSystem + StandaloneInputModule in an Input System-only project

Guideline: Place primary actions in the thumb zone of portrait games
Description: One-handed play: the main action is reachable without shifting grip
Do: Put play, buy and confirm buttons in the bottom third of the screen; keep rarely used actions (settings, close) at the top
Don't: Primary action button at the top of a portrait screen
Code Good: Play/Confirm anchored bottom-center above the safe area
Code Bad: Main CTA anchored to the top bar

Guideline: Avoid Layout Groups and Animators on dynamic UI
Description: Each change in a Layout Group dirties the whole chain; an Animator dirties its element every frame
Do: Use anchors for static layout, run a Layout Group once then disable it, and animate UI from code (tweens) instead of Animator
Don't: Nested HorizontalLayoutGroup/VerticalLayoutGroup/ContentSizeFitter on elements that change every frame
Code Good: layoutGroup.enabled = false after the first layout pass; tween scale/alpha in code
Code Bad: Animator on a static HUD panel; nested Layout Groups under a live score counter

Guideline: Fill the Android notch cutout but keep UI inside the safe area
Description: Full-bleed background on phones with a display cutout (notch / punch-hole) without hiding buttons under it
Do: Enable Player Settings > Resolution and Presentation > Render outside safe area (Android; editor setting, not runtime code) so the game draws into the cutout, then clamp the UI root to Screen.safeArea in a runtime script and re-apply it when the safe area changes (rotation)
Don't: Letterboxed black bar beside the notch, or HUD buttons placed under the camera cutout
Code Good: var a = Screen.safeArea; root.anchorMin = new Vector2(a.xMin / Screen.width, a.yMin / Screen.height); root.anchorMax = new Vector2(a.xMax / Screen.width, a.yMax / Screen.height);
Code Bad: Full-screen HUD anchored to the raw screen edges on a punch-hole Android phone

Guideline: Localize UI text with TMP fallback fonts
Description: Vietnamese diacritics and CJK glyphs render instead of empty boxes, and translated labels fit
Do: Localize strings with the Unity Localization package (string tables), give the TMP font asset fallback font assets for Vietnamese and CJK, leave 30-40% room for longer translations, and never bake text into sprites
Don't: Hardcoded English strings and one Latin-only font asset; text drawn into button images
Code Bad: label.text = "Play" with a Latin-only SDF font

Guideline: Bake 3D Blender Sprites for Juicy UI and Props
Description: Eliminate cheap flat 2D placeholders and give visual depth
Do: Render 3D beveled models (coins, gems, chests, trophies) in Blender with 3-point studio lighting and transparent alpha to 512x512 PNG, pack into SpriteAtlas
Don't: Flat single-color rectangles or unshaded primitive cubes for game rewards
Code Bad: Raw flat 2D square image with black border

Guideline: Apply squash and stretch on pointer down and up
Description: Give tactile bounce and organic elasticity to buttons
Do: Scale 0.92x on Y and 1.05x on X on pointer down (0.08s); bounce back with 1.08x overshoot easeOutBack on release (0.15s)
Don't: Static flat click with color tint only
Code Bad: button.image.color = Color.gray;

Guideline: Use non-linear trauma decay camera shake for impacts
Description: Realistic screen shake feel that scales quadratically
Do: Track Trauma in [0, 1]; shake amplitude = Trauma^2 * MaxOffset * PerlinNoise(seed, time); decay trauma linearly by 1.2/s
Don't: Random.insideUnitSphere added directly to camera position
Code Good: trauma = Mathf.Min(1f, trauma + 0.4f); float shake = trauma * trauma; cam.localPosition = originalPos + new Vector3(Mathf.PerlinNoise(0, t), Mathf.PerlinNoise(1, t)) * maxOffset * shake;
Code Bad: cam.transform.position += Random.insideUnitSphere * 0.5f;

Guideline: Configure URP Global Volume with ACES tonemapping and subtle bloom
Description: Eliminate blown-out highlights and give cinematic color depth
Do: Add Global Volume with Tonemapping (ACES), Bloom (Threshold 1.15, Scatter 0.7), Vignette (Intensity 0.22), Color Adjustments (Contrast +12, Saturation +8)
Don't: Raw unadjusted camera rendering with blown-out neon colors
Code Bad: Camera with default gamma rendering and no post-processing volume

Guideline: Enforce 60-30-10 color palette ratio and semantic colors
Description: Visual hierarchy prevents eye fatigue and guides player action
Do: 60% base neutral (dark slate #1A1A2E), 30% structural frame (golden bronze #C5A059), 10% high-contrast accent CTA (vivid emerald #00E676 or amber #FFA000)
Don't: Random saturated rainbow colors across all UI panels
Code Bad: Every button a different saturated primary color with no visual hierarchy

Guideline: Keep custom UI and VFX shaders SRP Batcher compatible
Description: Maintain high framerates and low draw calls on mobile URP
Do: Pack all material uniform properties into CBUFFER_START(UnityPerMaterial) ... CBUFFER_END; use half precision for colors/normals/UVs
Don't: Loose uniforms outside constant buffer breaking SRP Batcher
Code Bad: float4 _Color; declared in global scope outside CBUFFER

Guideline: Decouple UI and interaction SFX via Audio Event Bus with pitch jitter
Description: Prevent audio monotony and ear fatigue during rapid player interactions
Do: Dispatch events via AudioEventBus; play one-shots with random pitch offset between 0.95 and 1.05
Don't: Directly calling AudioSource.Play() on UI button click with fixed pitch
Code Bad: button.GetComponent<AudioSource>().Play(); with static 1.0 pitch

Guideline: No Panel inside Panel
Description: Do not stack a framed Panel inside another framed Panel. Separate groups with whitespace and a thin divider.
Do: One frame per screen region; spacing plus a 1 px divider between groups
Don't: A bordered Panel holding a bordered Panel holding a bordered Panel
Code Good: // one Panel per region; groups split by an Image 1 px tall tinted with the Divider token
Code Bad: Panel > Panel > Panel, each with its own border and shadow

Guideline: No icon tile above a heading
Description: Do not wrap an icon in a rounded pale square stacked above a title. Put the icon inline with the text or drop the frame.
Do: Icon inline in the heading row
Don't: A rounded pale square holding an icon above the heading
Code Bad: VerticalLayoutGroup: [RoundedSquare(icon)][TMP heading]

Guideline: Tinted neutrals: no bare #808080, no purple-blue gradient
Description: Greys carry 3-5% of the main hue. Never ship the bare mid grey #808080 or the stock purple-to-blue gradient.
Do: A tinted neutral derived from the brand colour, gradients built from brand tones
Don't: Pure grey #808080 or a purple-to-blue gradient copied from a template
Code Good: Color32 textMuted = new Color32(0x8A, 0x90, 0xA0, 0xFF); // grey with a few percent of the brand blue
Code Bad: Color textMuted = Color.gray; // 0.5, 0.5, 0.5

Guideline: Spacing rhythm 4-8 / 12-16 / 24-32, never 16 everywhere
Description: Space related items 4-8, content inside a frame 12-16 and sections 24-32 (reference pixels). One uniform 16 flattens the hierarchy.
Do: Three spacing tokens: group 8, content 16, section 32
Don't: The same 16 on every padding and spacing
Code Bad: everyLayout.spacing = 16;

Guideline: Tactile 9-slice buttons with a pressed sink
Description: A game button needs visible thickness (9-slice bevel) and a held pressed pose: scale 0.95 and a 2-4 px sink, restored on release. The squash tween of row 22 is the motion on pointer down; this is the pose the button holds. A flat web-style button reads as cheap.
Do: 9-slice sprite with bevel highlight and bottom shadow; while held scale 0.95 and sink 2-4 px; restore both on release
Don't: A flat borderless rectangle that only changes colour
Code Good: OnPointerDown: rt.localScale = Vector3.one * 0.95f; rt.anchoredPosition = rest + Vector2.down * 3f; OnPointerUp: rt.localScale = Vector3.one; rt.anchoredPosition = rest;
Code Bad: image.color = pressedColor; // flat web-style button

Guideline: Never ship the default LiberationSans SDF
Description: Game UI text uses a TMP font asset picked for the game's genre, never TextMeshPro's default LiberationSans SDF.
Do: A genre-matched TMP SDF font asset with an outline and drop-shadow preset
Don't: The default LiberationSans SDF on titles and buttons
Code Bad: tmp.font = TMP_Settings.defaultFontAsset; // LiberationSans SDF
